angularDiameterSource: Computed here from the record's radius and distance: 2 x 525,833 km at 79.40 pc = 0.09 mas. No interferometric diameter of this star is used.
distanceSource: Gaia DR3 parallax 12.5945 +/- 0.0127 mas (same row, RUWE 0.99): 79.40 pc, no zero-point correction
radiusSource: Radius 0.755833 solar radii from Lafarga et al. 2026, the stellar radius of the default parameter set of TOI-1105 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2026MNRAS.548ag512L/abstract): 525,833 km at 695,700 km per solar radius. Mass 0.737 (0.697 to 0.777) from Gaia DR3 FLAME (Creevey et al. 2023, A&A 674, A26; astrophysical_parameters of the same source); GM is that mass times the JPL solar GM. Temperature 4678.46 K from Lafarga et al. 2026, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of TOI-1105 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2026MNRAS.548ag512L/abstract). presentationUp: the display axis is a sky-plane convention; the spin axis's position angle on the sky is not measured.
effectiveTemperatureSource: Lafarga et al. 2026, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of TOI-1105 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2026MNRAS.548ag512L/abstract)
surfaceGravitySource: log g from the mass and radius in packages/astronomy/data/bodies/toi-1105.json (sources in its physicalNotes), log10(GM/R^2) in cgs: 4.549, rounded to two decimals
luminositySource: NASA Exoplanet Archive, composite parameters of TOI-1105 (pscomppars): log10 of the luminosity in solar units -0.61342, from TICv8 (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2019AJ....158..138S/abstract)

shape.qualification: A sphere at the published radius, colored from the star's Gaia DR3 BP/RP spectrum (photometry/stellar-color.json); no image of the photosphere exists.
